strengths: The paper introduces a well-defined and highly practical concept of 'Instruction-Visual Complexity' (IV-Complexity), addressing a key limitation in current instruction-based image editing.
The proposed 'plan-then-execute' framework (RePlan) effectively combines the strong visual reasoning and grounding capabilities of modern VLMs with the generative fidelity of diffusion models.
The attention region injection mechanism is elegant, training-free, and specifically tailored to MMDiT architectures, allowing for precise, multi-region parallel edits in a single pass.

The application of Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to fine-tune the VLM planner using only 1k instruction-only samples is exceptionally data-efficient and successfully improves structured output formatting and reasoning.
The newly proposed IV-Edit benchmark is comprehensive, categorizing diverse referring styles and complex editing task types, making it a valuable resource for future research.
weaknesses: The attention manipulation mechanism is highly specialized for the MMDiT architecture (where text, image, and latent tokens share a unified self-attention space). Its applicability to other widely used diffusion architectures (e.g., standard U-Net or DiT models with decoupled cross-attention) is limited.

The localization is based on bounding boxes (bboxes), which are inherently rectangular. For highly irregular or diagonally oriented objects, a bbox will inevitably contain a large amount of background, potentially leading to unwanted edits or blending artifacts.

The evaluation protocol relies almost entirely on Gemini-2.5-Pro as a judge. While automated LLM/VLM evaluations are common, a user study or human evaluation would make the quantitative comparisons on the new benchmark significantly more robust.

strengths: The paper introduces a well-designed 'plan-then-execute' framework (RePlan) that effectively leverages the reasoning power of VLMs to guide diffusion-based image editing, specifically addressing instruction-visual complexity.

The proposed attention region injection mechanism is training-free and elegant. By designing specific attention rules for MMDiT, it successfully prevents instruction leakage and allows parallel multi-region editing in a single pass.

The application of GRPO reinforcement learning is highly effective and sample-efficient, demonstrating that the VLM planner's formatting and reasoning capabilities can be significantly improved with only 1k instruction-only samples.
The paper introduces the IV-Edit benchmark, which is well-structured and focuses on complex reasoning and referring tasks, providing a valuable asset for future research in image editing.
Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate the clear superiority of RePlan in both target grounding and consistency compared to recent strong baselines and proprietary models.
weaknesses: The pipeline is highly dependent on the correctness of the VLM planner. If the VLM generates inaccurate bounding boxes or incorrect editing hints, the downstream diffusion editor will execute the incorrect plan with no way to recover.

The evaluation relies heavily on Gemini-2.5-Pro as the primary judge. While VLM-based evaluation is practical for complex instruction-based editing, a user study or human correlation analysis would strengthen the validity of the results.

The proposed attention manipulation is specifically tailored to MMDiT (Multimodal Diffusion Transformer) architectures. It is unclear how easily this can be adapted to other popular UNet-based diffusion backbones.

Comparison on more standard, widely used image editing benchmarks (e.g., MagicBrush, Emu Edit) is missing, which makes it harder to assess how the model performs on simpler or general-purpose editing tasks relative to existing models.

strengths: The framework of combining a VLM as a reasoning planner with an attention-directed diffusion model (MMDiT) for parallel, multi-region editing is logically designed and addresses the region-bleeding/spillover problems of global image editors.
The proposed training-free attention-region injection mechanism on MMDiT (Flux) is elegant and bypasses the need for training or fine-tuning heavy diffusion parameters.

Utilizing Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to fine-tune the planner's formatting and spatial accuracy with only 1k samples is a clever and computationally efficient way to bootstrap VLM planning.
The paper is well-written, with clear figures (particularly Figure 4 visualizing the attention masking rules) and detailed appendix documentation.
weaknesses: Circular Evaluation Bias: The dataset (IV-Edit) was constructed using Gemini 2.5 Pro (to select images, choose category combinations, and construct editing instructions), and the final quantitative evaluation (Table 1) relies entirely on Gemini 2.5 Pro as the evaluator. Evaluating a model on a dataset generated by the same LLM/VLM engine introduces severe evaluation bias, as the evaluator is likely to favor outputs aligned with its own generation patterns.

Lack of Human Evaluation: Given the high complexity of the edits and the limitations of LLM-as-a-judge protocols, a rigorous human evaluation is crucial to validate the performance of RePlan against baselines. Relying solely on VLM metrics (Table 1) makes the claims less convincing.

Visual/Boundary Artifacts: Looking closely at the qualitative results, some edits exhibit visible boundary transitions and perspective/realism issues. For instance, in Figure 6 (column 2, bottom), the elephant's body integration with the background wall has noticeable artifacts. In Figure 1 (row 3, Pinocchio carrot), the extension looks highly distorted and cartoonish, lacking natural blending.

Missing Standard Benchmarks: While the authors construct the IV-Edit benchmark to highlight instruction-visual complexity, it would strengthen the paper to also report results on established instruction-based image editing benchmarks such as MagicBrush or HQ-Edit to demonstrate the generalizability of the proposed framework.
